Run from Bali.

We shoot the property. We build the walkthrough. We put both on a page a buyer can use. The studio is in Kerobokan, Kuta Utara.

Why this exists

A shoot without a page is a folder. A page without the shoot is a brochure. Too many briefs died in the gap between a drone operator, a production house, and a web shop. We keep the film, the tour, and the page in the same brief so the work actually lands.

Founder

Christobal Grego

He came to Bali in 2020 to build Meta Pacific, a real estate media studio. Film, FPV, virtual tours, and the pages that sell the place.

LinkedIn

What we do

FPV, film, photography, virtual tours. Then the landing page, and tracking so you can see who moved. Strategy if the story is still loose. Follow-up if the launch has to keep going after the first cut.

The work is for hospitality, villas, land, founders, and lifestyle brands. If the place or the person has to make sense on a phone before anyone books a flight, it is our kind of brief.

How we work

One team on the brief

The people who fly the site should be able to cut the film and wire the page. We do not hand you a folder and send you looking for the rest.

Show the place as it is

Terrain, access, rooms, light. A buyer should recognise the site when they arrive. We do not invent a sky.

Tools stay on the desk

AI is useful when it saves a round. It is not the look, and it does not get a credit on the work.

Sell the result, not the hours

A clearer property story. A page that can take a lead. You should be able to name what changed. Shot counts stay in our notes.

What we stand for.

Purpose, mission, vision, and the six standards we use on every brief.

Purpose

We exist so a property, a founder, or a brand can be understood, trusted, and sold without the work splitting across a drone supplier, a production house, a web agency, and a growth shop. Meta Pacific keeps those jobs in one practice, run from Bali, for clients who need the place or the person to be clear before anyone has to fly in.

Mission and vision

Mission

We take a commercial problem through the shoot, the page, and the system that follows.

We plan the story, produce the film and the walkthrough, build the page it lives on, and wire the tracking that shows whether anyone actually moved. The mission is a working path from first look to a named result, not a reel of isolated deliverables.

Vision

We want the work to be why a Bali project comes back.

Hospitality, villas, founders, and lifestyle brands should be able to trust one studio for film, page, and campaign. That reputation is built through finished work, not a longer service list.

Working standards

01

Start from the sale, not the shot list

The brief has to name what should change: more inquiries, a clearer property story, or a founder people already trust. If we cannot name the result, we do not start production.

02

Keep the stack in one practice

The team that flies the site should be able to cut the film, build the landing page, and wire the tracking. We do not hand a client a finished asset and leave them to find the rest elsewhere.

03

Show the place as it actually is

FPV, virtual tours, and property films exist to make terrain, access, and space readable. We do not dress a plot or a villa into something a buyer will not find when they arrive.

04

Use AI as a production tool

Automation and generation exist to move iteration faster. They do not replace art direction, references, or the eye that decides what ships. Being AI-made is not treated as an achievement.

05

Protect the visual identity

Every asset on a project has to hold the same look, whether it came from a camera, a walkthrough, or a generated pass. Taste is a filter on the work, not a mood board presented at kickoff.

06

Stay selective

We take projects where the commercial problem is real and the client wants the work connected. A single deliverable is available. A relationship that stops at isolated production hours is not the default.

Creative technology

AI effects vs. traditional VFX

Generation is a production tool. It does not replace the eye that decides what ships.

Traditional VFX is slow and expensive, and you can point at every frame and say who made the decision. Generative tools are fast, and they will happily invent a villa that does not exist. For property work that is not a feature. A buyer who arrives to a different roof line does not care that the model was impressive.

We use generation where it earns its keep: extending a plate, finishing a motion pass, iterating a graphic, illustrating an interview. We do not use it to dress a plot into a resort. That is one of the working standards on Our values.

The 3D render tour is the honest version of 'the building is not there yet.' It is labelled as a model because it is a model. AI that pretends to be a finished villa is a different product, and it is not this studio's.

If a generated pass cannot hold the same look as the live shoot, it does not ship. Art direction is the filter. Being AI-made is not treated as an achievement.

Drones / FPV

FPV vs. traditional drone for property marketing

One is for establishing the site. The other is for moving through it. Most launches need both.

A conventional drone is a viewpoint. It tells you where the project sits in the landscape, how far the sea is, and how the massing reads from above. That is the establishing shot. Without it, an FPV clip can feel like a corridor with no map.

FPV is a path. It is how you arrive, how you move between buildings, and how a villa or a plot is actually used. Sakti and Mini Map are this job: terrain and access. Sardine Rote and Villa Koh Samui are this job for hospitality: would you walk this place.

We do not pick a toy and then find a use for it. If the blocked yes is 'I cannot tell how I get onto the land,' the flight follows the access. If the blocked yes is 'I cannot tell if I would stay here,' the flight follows the stay.

Anjuna Bay uses both on the same development: FPV for movement, a virtual tour for staying. That pairing is the default when a project has to sell before anyone flies in.

Property marketing

How virtual tours help sell villas before a physical visit

What buyers actually need to see before they book a flight, and what a flat photo set leaves out.

A still set can make a villa look expensive. It is bad at answering the questions that actually stop a flight: how you enter, how the rooms connect, what you see from the bed, and whether the place is the size it claimed to be.

A virtual tour is not a nicer gallery. It is a way for someone in another country to walk the circulation themselves. If they cannot find the kitchen from the living room, they will not find it when they arrive either. That is useful information before anyone buys a ticket.

The tours in our work are built for that job. Anjuna Bay and K-Club Ubud are not mood pieces. They are spatial records a buyer can steer. Pre-construction work, like the 3D render tour, does the same thing when the building is still a model.

A tour that dies in an email attachment still fails. It has to sit on a page, next to a way to ask for a viewing. Virtual tours is the capture. Web and landing pages is where the walkthrough becomes a lead.

Questions developers ask.

What does a developer launch include?

The open offer is virtual tour, FPV walkthrough, aerial footage, a sales-oriented property film, and short-form social assets. The landing page and tracking sit in the same brief when the project needs a place for the lead to land.

How does pricing work?

The Immersive Property Launch has a published reference price of IDR 25,000,000 for one launch system. Scope can change it. Ongoing work across overlapping sites is quoted after a review. We do not invent a monthly number before we have seen the sites.

Can you run more than one site at a time?

Yes. That is the usual shape of a developer brief. Capture is planned so overlapping launches still share a look. We take the work we can keep consistent. We do not stack sites until the look breaks.

Do you work outside Bali?

The studio is in Kerobokan. Selected work includes Nusa Penida, East Nusa Tenggara, and Koh Samui. Permits and access are confirmed before we fly.

What if the building is not finished?

That is a normal brief. We tour from the site as it stands, and from 3D renders when the rooms do not exist yet. A buyer should still recognise the place when they arrive.

What happens after the first cut?

You review the cuts and the tour before anything is treated as final. Changes that stay inside the agreed brief are part of delivery. A new site, a new story, or a second launch is a new scope.

Do we have to manage the production?

No. Send the brief. We answer on WhatsApp. Reviews happen on the cuts and tours, not on a call for every frame. You should not need to run three suppliers to get a film, a walkthrough, and a page.

Drone and FPV

Aerial establishing shots and FPV walkthroughs used to make terrain, access, and space readable.

Who it is for

  • Land and development projects that cannot be judged from a gate photo.
  • Resorts and villas that need the approach and the layout understood in one pass.

Problems it solves

  • Buyers cannot tell how the site sits, how you enter it, or what the rooms actually connect to.
  • A pretty aerial that does not help anyone decide.

Scope

  • Aerial establishing shots
  • FPV walkthroughs and spatial tours
  • Landscape and architecture from the air
  • Cuts that can live on a page, in a tour, or as short-form

Not included

  • Stunts for their own sake. FPV is a storytelling tool, not a gimmick.
  • A flight with no plan for where the footage will sell.

Deliverables

  • FPV walkthrough
  • Aerial plates
  • Short-form cuts from the same flight

01

Flight plan

Path, height, and what the viewer must understand.

02

Capture

Cut

Do you fly in Thailand and Nusa Penida as well as Bali?

The selected work includes those places. We confirm permits and access before we fly.
